title: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself 🪶
description:
Try to tickle yourself: nothing happens. Your brain predicts exactly what your own fingers will feel and turns the feeling down. Scientists proved it with a tickle robot: add a delay of just a fifth of a second and the tickle comes back.

Are you ticklish?

Sources: Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith, "Central cancellation of self-produced tickle sensation", Nature Neuroscience 1, 635 (1998); Blakemore, Frith & Wolpert, "Spatio-temporal prediction modulates the perception of self-produced stimuli", Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience 11, 551 (1999); Scientific American, "Why can't a person tickle himself?".
Animation and music: TrueWhys (original).
TrueWhys — the real story behind life's weirdest whys.
